SALONE Public Resource Management for Jobs and Growth PforR
boards.abstract: The SALONE Public Resource Management for Jobs and Growth Program-for-Results (PforR) supports Sierra Leone’s public financial management reform agenda by addressing key institutional constraints underlying the country’s fiscal challenges. The Program is anchored in the Government’s PFM Reform Strategy (2023–2030), Medium-Term Revenue Strategy, and Medium-Term Debt Strategy, and focuses on strengthening the effective implementation and sustained use of existing systems and reforms. Its development objective is to increase domestic revenue, improve the credibility of public spending, and strengthen debt management in Sierra Leone.The US$36 million PforR is structured around three Results Areas:(i) increasing domestic revenue; (ii) improving the credibility of public spending; and (iii) strengthening debt management, supported by eight Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs).Key areas of support include:- Strengthening revenue administration and taxpayer compliance by increasing the use of Electronic Cash Register (ECR) data to verify domestic output GST and improving timely filing and payment by large and medium taxpayers, supported by improved system interoperability, data sharing, and risk-based compliance monitoring and enforcement.- Improving budget credibility and expenditure control by strengthening IFMIS-based commitment controls, improving the timeliness and predictability of quarterly budget releases to health and education, and reducing expenditure composition variance between approved budgets and actual spending across covered MDAs.- Increasing transparency, competition, and accountability in public spending through expanded end-to-end use of e-GP, stronger enforcement of procurement requirements, greater interoperability between e-GP and IFMIS, improved disclosure of procurement information, and more systematic implementation and verification of external audit recommendations across MDAs and Local Councils.- Strengthening debt and arrears management by reducing the stock of central government and SOE arrears and strengthening fiscal and expenditure controls to prevent the accumulation of new arrears. Complementary technical assistance will also support the credibility and implementation of the Government’s Annual Borrowing Plan.The Program has nationwide coverage and is expected to benefit citizens, taxpayers, the private sector, and public institutions through stronger fiscal management, more predictable and transparent public spending, improved accountability, and reduced fiscal risks. Its contribution to service delivery is primarily through stronger upstream PFM systems, including more predictable financing for health and education.The PforR is complemented by a US$4 million IPF component providing targeted technical assistance and implementation support. Sub-Component A (US$2 million) supports parliamentary oversight; civil society engagement and grants; technical assistance for key PFM reforms, including audit follow-up, procurement, debt management, and climate- and gender-responsive public investment management; and a learning agenda linked to the regional MPA. Sub-Component B (US$2 million) supports Program implementation and coordination within PFMRD, including specialized capacity for financial management, monitoring and evaluation, environmental and social risk management, and internal audit, as well as data quality assurance and the procurement of an Independent Verification Agent. The support is designed to strengthen existing PFMRD arrangements rather than establish a parallel PIU.

boards.name: Liberia Forest Economy Project (LiFE-P)
boards.abstract: This project seeks to capitalize on the former Liberia Forest Sector Project’s achievements and lessons learned to boost Liberia’s forest economy and to meet its NDC targets by improving the governance of the forestry sector, the interventions related to conservation, and commercial activities, and the participation of communities’ vis a vis income generation and alternative livelihoods. The World Bank’s Global Challenge on Forests for Development, Climate and Biodiversity (GCP-F) provides a framework for addressing key challenges of Liberia's forestry sector improving the lives of people living in and around forests and bringing a cohesive framework for national commitments. It can provide the foundation for a long-term forest economy as well as the foundation for climate financing.
